**Course Description**  
**Faculty of Shari'ah**  
**PhD in the Islamic Creed**

**0431933 Islamic Philosophy** (3 credit hours)  
This course deals with the origins of modern philosophy and how it relates to Islamic thought and the views of Muslim philosophers, their beliefs, affiliations, and beliefs.

**0401937 Creed of General Muslims (1)** (3 credit hours)  
This course provides an in-depth study of the Qur'anic and Prophetic approach to creed matters, the method by which the Companions received the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and the methodology they eventually adopted. It examines how followers dealt with creed matters until the rise of groups that discussed the subject of creed and the methodology the scholars adopted in answering these groups and confirming the creed.

**0401938 Creed of General Muslims (2)** (3 credit hours)  
This course offers an in-depth study of the reasons behind the rise of the Ash'ari and Maturidi schools, the most significant creed matters they dealt with, and the reasons for the emergence of this method and their efforts in writing back to the Mu'tazilites, the disbelievers, and other groups. Furthermore, the course discusses the most distinguished scholars in the two schools in the past and present.

**0401939 Studies in Islamic Sects** (3 credit hours)  
This course includes a detailed study of Hadith of separation, the internal and external reasons for the survival of some sects and the extinction of others. It studies the most distinguished issues related to these groups, such as Imamate, Atakfir, Ataw'il, Assifat, and Al-Ma'ad. The course also addresses groups like Al-Kawarij, Ash'ari, Al-Murji'ah, Al-Kadareah, Al-Jabreh, Al-Mu'attilah (Al-Jahmiah), Al-Mushabbisihah, and Al-Mu'tazilah.

**0401940 Issues in Theological Rhetoric (Kalam)** (3 credit hours)  
This course examines the definition of theological rhetoric, the factors behind its rise, the phases of its development, its legal ruling, the scholars' positions on it in the past and present, and the need for it.
